title: Descent of homotopies between affine perfect chain maps
statement: Let I be a directed preorder, F : I → CRing a functor, i₀ ∈ I, and A the colimit of F [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let E₀ and K₀ be cochain complexes of F(i₀)-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], each zero outside a finite interval and with each term finitely generated and projective. For i ≥ i₀ write Eᵢ and Kᵢ for their termwise scalar extensions along F(i₀ → i), and E and K for their termwise extensions along the colimit inclusion F(i₀) → A. For base-change maps between these complexes, use the canonical associativity transport [def-pc-complex-scalar-extension-hom]. Given i ≥ i₀ and chain maps f,g : Eᵢ → Kᵢ whose scalar extensions to A are homotopic, there exists j ≥ i and a homotopy between the scalar extensions of f and g to Eⱼ → Kⱼ.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 36.29.2, Tag 09RE, affine proof

proof.text: Choose a homotopy over A. Its degree-minus-one components have source Eⁿ and target Kⁿ⁻¹ and only finitely many components can be nonzero. Finite projectivity implies finite presentation by Mathlib Module.finitePresentation_of_projective. Descend these components by [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine] and take a common upper stage above i. In a preorder the same finite-presentation proof applies, using the elementwise colimit criterion [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise]; no use of antisymmetry is made. To use the stated partial-order theorem literally, quotient I by mutual comparability and select representatives. The resulting partial-order category is equivalent to I; F sends mutually comparable indices to inverse isomorphisms, so transport F and its colimit across this equivalence, apply the partial-order theorem, and transport the finite-data result back. Directedness supplies an upper bound with the original requested index.

At the stage where the components are defined, the homotopy equations fⁿ - gⁿ = d_K sⁿ + sⁿ⁺¹ d_E hold over A. Apply equality detection to each of the finitely many nontrivial equations, and take a common later upper bound j. Put zero components outside the support and away from the required degree-minus-one shape. The homotopy identities then hold in every degree. Canonical associativity transport identifies the two endpoint maps with scalarExtensionHom, giving the required Nonempty Homotopy at j.

lean.statement: theorem affine_perfect_homotopy_descent {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (i₀ : I) (E₀ K₀ : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} (F.obj i₀)) ℤ) (hE : (∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (E₀.X n)) ∧ ∀ n : ℤ, Module.Finite (F.obj i₀) (E₀.X n) ∧ Module.Projective (F.obj i₀) (E₀.X n)) (hK : (∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (K₀.X n)) ∧ ∀ n : ℤ, Module.Finite (F.obj i₀) (K₀.X n) ∧ Module.Projective (F.obj i₀) (K₀.X n)) (i : Set.Ici i₀) (f g : ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (F.map (homOfLE i.property)).hom).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj E₀ ⟶ ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (F.map (homOfLE i.property)).hom).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj K₀) (h : Nonempty (Homotopy (scalarExtensionHom (F.map (homOfLE i.property)).hom (colimit.ι F i.val).hom (colimit.ι F i₀).hom (congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom (colimit.w F (homOfLE i.property)).symm) E₀ K₀ f) (scalarExtensionHom (F.map (homOfLE i.property)).hom (colimit.ι F i.val).hom (colimit.ι F i₀).hom (congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom (colimit.w F (homOfLE i.property)).symm) E₀ K₀ g))) : ∃ (j : Set.Ici i₀) (hij : i ≤ j), Nonempty (Homotopy (scalarExtensionHom (F.map (homOfLE i.property)).hom (F.map (homOfLE hij)).hom (F.map (homOfLE j.property)).hom (congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom (F.map_comp (homOfLE i.property) (homOfLE hij))) E₀ K₀ f) (scalarExtensionHom (F.map (homOfLE i.property)).hom (F.map (homOfLE hij)).hom (F.map (homOfLE j.property)).hom (congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom (F.map_comp (homOfLE i.property) (homOfLE hij))) E₀ K₀ g))
